home.status.label: Project status
home.status.heading: Early design phase
home.status.body: There is no released application yet. The project currently consists of design documents, draft interface specifications and automated checks.
docs.overviewBody: The planned application connects to the game through the official SCS telemetry SDK, reads vehicle data, and sends steering, throttle and brake commands through a virtual controller. A separate desktop interface shows status and lets the driver start and stop assistance.
docs.requirementsBody: Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit) and Euro Truck Simulator 2. Exact game versions and other prerequisites will be published with the first release.
docs.installBody: No installer or download exists yet. Installation steps will be added when a release is published.
docs.troubleshootingBody: Troubleshooting guidance will be added once there is an application to troubleshoot.
architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.description: How the planned modules fit together and the safety rules they share.
architecture.heading: Architecture
architecture.intro: The project is split into modules with clear responsibilities. Modules communicate only through versioned interface contracts. This is a draft design; nothing described here is implemented yet.
architecture.diagramTitle: Planned data flow between the game and the project's modules
architecture.diagramDesc: The game provides vehicle data to a telemetry plugin through the official SCS telemetry SDK. The plugin shares it with the Python core. The core sends control commands to the input module, which applies them to the game through a virtual controller. A desktop interface exchanges status and requests with the core.
architecture.flow.one: The game provides vehicle data through the official SCS telemetry SDK to the telemetry plugin.
architecture.flow.two: The telemetry plugin publishes the data to the core through shared memory.
architecture.flow.three: The core sends steering, throttle and brake commands to the input module through a named pipe.
architecture.flow.four: The input module applies the commands to the game through a virtual controller.
architecture.flow.five: The desktop interface exchanges status and requests with the core through a second named pipe.
architecture.module.plugin.name: Telemetry plugin
architecture.module.plugin.role: Loads into the game as an SCS SDK plugin and publishes vehicle data to shared memory.
architecture.module.input.name: Input module
architecture.module.input.role: Applies steering, throttle and brake commands through a virtual controller. It does not decide the commands.
architecture.module.core.name: Core
architecture.module.core.role: Perception, planning, the control loop and safety limits. It does not access game memory directly.
architecture.module.ui.name: Desktop interface
architecture.module.ui.role: Settings, status, start and stop, and logs. It does not run the control loop.
architecture.safetyIntro: These principles are part of the draft design and are not yet implemented.
architecture.safety.one: The driver always wins: any manual steering, throttle or brake input takes priority and disengages assistance.
architecture.safety.two: Commands are limited in range and in rate twice: once in the core and again in the input module.
architecture.safety.three: If fresh, valid commands stop arriving within a short time limit, the input module sets all outputs to zero and disengages.
architecture.safety.four: After a disconnect, a timeout or a manual override, assistance never resumes by itself; the driver must request it again.
architecture.safety.five: The desktop interface only requests actions and shows status. It never runs the control loop.
